title: Qu'est-ce qu'un nombre?
oneGoal: Students recognize that numbers are everywhere in their world
decisionPoints: How are students feeling about learning in French today?
What level of English scaffolding is needed?
Should we extend the number hunt or move to circle time?
progression: Foundation lesson - activating prior knowledge about numbers in their environment

title: Compter ensemble
oneGoal: Students can count from 0 to 5 with objects
decisionPoints: Are students ready for individual counting or need more group support?
Should we focus on 0-3 or extend to 5?
What manipulatives are most engaging today?
progression: Builds on number recognition by introducing sequential counting with concrete objects

title: Voir les nombres
oneGoal: Students recognize dot patterns for numbers 1-3 without counting
decisionPoints: Can students subitize 1-2 or are they ready for 3?
Should we use dot cards, dominoes, or both?
Is the pace too fast or too slow for the group?
progression: Develops visual number recognition building on counting skills from lesson 2

title: Plus de nombres
oneGoal: Students can count and recognize patterns for numbers 6-8
decisionPoints: Are students confident with 0-5 before moving forward?
Should we focus on just 6-7 or include 8?
What concrete materials help most with these larger numbers?
progression: Extends counting range while maintaining visual pattern recognition from lesson 3

title: Compter en arrière
oneGoal: Students can count backwards from 5 to 0
decisionPoints: Should we start from 3, 4, or 5 for backwards counting?
Are physical movements helping or distracting?
Do students need more practice with forward counting first?
progression: Introduces reverse counting building on forward counting confidence from lessons 1-4

title: Neuf et dix
oneGoal: Students recognize and count to 10 using various representations
decisionPoints: Are students ready for 10 or should we focus on 9?
Which representations (fingers, objects, pictures) work best?
Should we practice more 0-8 review or move forward?
progression: Completes the 0-10 number sequence building on all previous counting work

title: Patterns de points
oneGoal: Students quickly recognize dot patterns for 4-6 without counting
decisionPoints: Can students handle 4-5 patterns or need to stay with 1-3?
Should we use ten frames, dice, or dot cards?
Are students guessing or truly recognizing patterns?
progression: Extends subitizing skills from lesson 3 to larger numbers using systematic patterns

title: Comparer les groupes
oneGoal: Students compare groups using words 'plus que' and 'moins que'
decisionPoints: Should we compare groups of 1-5 or extend to 1-8?
Are students ready for 'égal' or focus on more/less?
What concrete materials make comparisons clearest?
progression: Introduces comparison concepts using counting and recognition skills from previous lessons

title: Dix cadre magique
oneGoal: Students use ten frames to represent numbers 1-10
decisionPoints: Should we start with 1-5 on the ten frame or go to 10?
Are students filling randomly or systematically?
Do we need more practice with smaller numbers first?
progression: Introduces ten frames as a key tool for organizing number knowledge from all previous lessons

title: Grands patterns
oneGoal: Students recognize patterns for 7-10 using ten frames and other arrangements
decisionPoints: Can students handle 7-10 patterns or need more 4-6 practice?
Should we focus on ten frames or include other arrangements?
Are students seeing patterns or still counting everything?
progression: Extends pattern recognition to larger numbers using ten frame organization from lesson 9

title: Résoudre des problèmes
oneGoal: Students solve simple comparison problems using manipulatives and referents
decisionPoints: Should problems involve numbers 1-5, 1-8, or 1-10?
Are students ready for word problems or need visual problems?
What referents (fingers, ten frame, objects) are most helpful?
progression: Applies all counting, recognition, and comparison skills to solve contextualized problems

title: Compter partout
oneGoal: Students demonstrate counting skills from 0-20 and backwards from 10
decisionPoints: Can students count to 15, 20, or stay with 10?
Should we count by 1s, or introduce skip counting?
Are students ready for assessment or need more practice?
progression: Extends counting range beyond 10 while consolidating all previous counting skills

title: Montrer ce que je sais
oneGoal: Students demonstrate recognition of arrangements 1-10 and solve comparison problems
decisionPoints: Which students need more support vs. challenge?
Should assessment be individual, paired, or small group?
Are students ready to explain their thinking in French?
progression: Consolidates pattern recognition and problem-solving skills for formal assessment

title: Célébrer les nombres
oneGoal: Students demonstrate complete understanding of counting and number concepts 0-10
decisionPoints: Which concepts need final reinforcement?
Should celebration include games, songs, or demonstrations?
Are all curriculum expectations sufficiently covered?
progression: Final core lesson ensuring all curriculum expectations are met through celebration and demonstration

title: Jeux de nombres
oneGoal: Students practice number recognition through engaging games
decisionPoints: Which games are most engaging for this group?
Should we focus on recognition speed or accuracy?
Are students ready for competitive games or keep it collaborative?
progression: Extension lesson providing additional practice with number recognition through play

title: Histoire de nombres
oneGoal: Students create and share stories using numbers 0-10
decisionPoints: Should stories be verbal, drawn, or acted out?
Are students ready to create individually or in pairs?
How can we support French language production?
progression: Extension providing creative application of number knowledge through storytelling

title: Chasse aux nombres
oneGoal: Students find and document numbers in their school environment
decisionPoints: Should the hunt be in classroom, hallway, or outside?
Are students ready to work independently or need partners?
How will students record their findings?
progression: Extension connecting number knowledge to real-world contexts beyond the classroom

title: Art de nombres
oneGoal: Students create artistic representations of numbers using various materials
decisionPoints: Should we use paint, collage, playdough, or digital tools?
Are students ready to choose their own numbers or assign them?
How much time should be spent on creation vs. sharing?
progression: Extension integrating number concepts with creative expression and fine motor skills

title: Défis de comptage
oneGoal: Students engage in challenging counting activities and puzzles
decisionPoints: Should challenges involve counting by 2s, backwards, or mixed sequences?
Are students ready for timed challenges or keep it pressure-free?
Which students need easier vs. harder challenges?
progression: Extension providing additional challenge and practice for advanced counting skills

title: Fête des nombres
oneGoal: Students celebrate their number learning journey through multiple activities
decisionPoints: Should the celebration include stations, performances, or games?
Are families invited or is this a class celebration?
How can students demonstrate growth from lesson 1 to now?
progression: Final extension lesson celebrating the complete learning journey and growth in number understanding
